Part D omitted — this exercise forbade opening any reading. Answered only from documented biography (Wikipedia, Britannica, CBC, Globe and Mail, Global News, Time, his memoir 'Common Ground' as reported, Find a Grave/WikiTree for grandparents' dates, the Immelman personality-profile paper). No astrology source was searched, opened, or reasoned from; one astrology-site result surfaced incidentally in a personality search and was discarded unread.

DOCUMENTED, high confidence: born 25 Dec 1971, 9:27 pm EST, Ottawa Civic Hospital (A1/A2/B5) — the minute-level time comes from contemporary press reporting of the hospital announcement, which is why A1='hospital' and A2='exact'; no rectification is on the biographical record (A3='no', but absence of evidence). Eldest of three sons of Pierre and Margaret Trudeau (B4); brothers Alexandre 'Sacha' (b. 1973) and Michel (1975–1998, killed in an avalanche at Kokanee Glacier Park 13 Nov 1998, body never recovered) — hence A13='lost'. Half-siblings Kyle (1984) and Alicia (1988) Kemper and Sarah Coyne (1991). Education: Rockcliffe Park PS, Collège Jean-de-Brébeuf, BA Literature McGill 1994, B.Ed UBC 1998 (A14='graduate'); engineering at École Polytechnique de Montréal 2002–04 and an MA in Environmental Geography at McGill both abandoned — that is the basis for A15='brief' and for including metals_machinery in A18. Careers: substitute then permanent teacher (French, math, drama, social studies) at West Point Grey Academy, Vancouver, from 1998/99 (salary_private); nightclub bouncer, snowboard and whitewater instructor, camp counsellor, radio host; chair of Katimavik 2002–06 (charitable — basis for 'religious' in A18); actor in CBC's 'The Great War' (2007) and memoirist (design_art, writing_media); paid public-speaking business run through numbered companies (own_business, best year >$450k); MP for Papineau from 14 Oct 2008 and PM 4 Nov 2015 – 14 Mar 2025 (salary_government). A17='under_authority' because his entire success is inside elected/public office. A20='some' — his largest single income stream (MP/PM salary) was earned in Ottawa, his birthplace; teaching income and speaking fees were earned elsewhere in Canada. A22='significant' — c. CA$1.2m inheritance from Pierre's estate plus further 2016 distributions, Cormier House in Montreal and a ~50-hectare Laurentian estate; that also drives C5 and C7. A24='separated' — married Sophie Grégoire 28 May 2005, signed a legal separation agreement announced 2 Aug 2023; no divorce is documented, so 'divorced' would overstate. Children Xavier (18 Oct 2007), Ella-Grace (5 Feb 2009), Hadrien (28 Feb 2014). A36='much_worse': separation Aug 2023, approval 65% (2016) to 22% (Dec 2024), Freeland's resignation Dec 2024, resignation announced 6 Jan 2025, left office 14 Mar 2025, stood down at the 2025 election.

JUDGEMENT CALLS, flagged: A9 — grandparents are precisely dated (Charles-Émile Trudeau 1887–1935, d. 47; Grace Elliott Trudeau 1890–1973, d. ~83; James Sinclair 1908–1984, d. 75; Kathleen 'Bubbles' Sinclair 1920–2012, d. 92); the arithmetic mean is 74.25 so I answered 70_80 literally, but the 47–92 spread would equally justify 'mixed'. A11 — Pierre was PM for almost all of Justin's childhood and independently wealthy throughout, so 'steady'; the 1979 electoral defeat and nine months out of office is a real documented reversal that would justify 'reversal'. A12 — the adult relationship with Margaret is close and mutually supportive, but he describes her childhood absences after she moved out (he was 6) as 'traumatic' and describes consoling her at age 11; 'absent' is defensible for the childhood window only. A19='above' — a judgement, not a fact: he reached the highest office in Canada on a comparatively thin CV (teacher, seven years as a backbench/critic MP) and was widely commented on as elevated by name and celebrity. A26='on_time' — married at 33; his father married at 51 and his mother at 22, so the 'family pattern' is incoherent. A30 — sociable/bold rest on the Immelman profile (Outgoing/gregarious primary, Ambitious/confident secondary, Dauntless and Dominant subsidiary, 'energetic extravert'); quick_tempered rests on his own words ('I lost my temper') after calling Peter Kent a 'piece of shit' in the Commons in Dec 2011 and on Elbowgate, 18 May 2016; outspoken rests on the documented run of off-the-cuff gaffes. A31='brief' — he has said publicly he 'sought counselling on many occasions' and got help from therapists after Michel's and Pierre's deaths, but no diagnosis or treatment duration is on record, so 'extended' would be unsupported. A32='strong' — raised Catholic, self-described 'lapsed Catholic' by late adolescence, faith revived after Michel's death via an Alpha course ('trust in God's plan'); practising but explicitly separates church from his politics, so 'central' would overstate. B1 is the weakest item: opt1 chosen for his signature public emotionality and the mother-attachment thread that runs through both memoirs, but opt2 ('wants to be seen and respected, proud, does not take correction easily') is equally well documented — the peer-reviewed profile calls him adaptively narcissistic, and he publicly disputed the Ethics Commissioner's SNC-Lavalin finding rather than accept it. B3='younger' rests on the recurring 'boyish' characterisation, not on a survey. C12 at confidence 2 for the same reason: nine years as PM argues opt2, while four ethics findings and a Federal Court ruling argue the opposite, and no 'both' option exists.

GENUINELY UNDOCUMENTED after searching, answered conservatively: A4 (hospital admissions), A5 (surgeries), A6 (recurring body trouble) — nothing beyond two COVID-19 infections (Jan 2022, Jun 2022, both managed at home) is on the public record, so 'none'/'none'/'none' are floor answers, not positive findings. A7='average' and A8='no' — no childhood illness or near-death event before age 8 is documented anywhere I could find; 'unknown' was available for both and would also be honest. A21='never' — no speculation, betting or share trading is documented. A23='none' — no debt is documented. A29='no' — no fertility difficulty or child loss is documented. A34='never' — no institutional confinement; official residences (24 Sussex, Rideau Cottage) and COVID self-isolation are not confinement in the intended sense. C6 at confidence 2 because no sudden windfall distinct from the inheritance is on record.

EVENTS CAPPED AT 12 (A35). Omitted for space but equally real: parents' divorce finalised 2 Apr 1984; delivering Pierre's eulogy 3 Oct 2000 (the moment usually named as the start of his political life); boxing win over Sen. Patrick Brazeau 31 Mar 2012; memoir 'Common Ground' Oct 2014; births of Ella-Grace (Feb 2009) and Hadrien (Feb 2014); re-elected with minority governments 2019 and 2021. Reputational/legal history not codable in A35: Aga Khan island vacation — four-count Conflict of Interest Act violation, Dec 2017 (first sitting PM found to have broken federal conflict-of-interest law); SNC-Lavalin — s.9 violation, 14 Aug 2019; brownface/blackface photos published 18 Sep 2019; WE Charity, 2020 (investigated, cleared); Emergencies Act invoked Feb 2022, ruled unreasonable by the Federal Court 23 Jan 2024 and unlawful by the Federal Court of Appeal Jan 2026; Yaroslav Hunka ovation 22 Sep 2023; a 2000 Kokanee festival groping allegation resurfaced in 2018. Honours: honorary doctorates from Edinburgh (2017) and NYU (2018), Honorary Fellowship of the Royal Canadian Geographical Society. B6#2 uses 2000 for his mother's major illness — her severe breakdown followed Michel's death and Pierre's death, though the bipolar diagnosis was only made public on 5 May 2006; treat the year as soft.
